summary: First-principles design review (full record in review_loop/scrutiny_03.md). I articulated the falsifiable headline claim, re-derived the estimators, and pressed the design where a hostile reviewer would. Six substantive issues found and FIXED this iteration: (1) matched-k was enforced at run time only — compare() differenced each arm's diverse-pass@k at its OWN k, so any k divergence (failed resample, --max-k, capture loss) silently biased the gain toward the larger arm; now both arms are evaluated at the common per-instance k*=min(k_A,k_B) via the Chen estimator with k-mismatch reporting, demonstrated by a test where own-k says gain 0 and matched-k* correctly says -0.5. (2) Cross-arm distinct-patch counts had the same sample-size bias; fixed with the closed-form rarefaction estimator expected_distinct_at_k = sum_sig pass@k*(n, m_sig) (mean pairwise distance provably needs no correction — pair-inclusion symmetry — now documented). (3) Inference at n=10 rested on a percentile bootstrap over lumpy 0/1 gains; added the EXACT paired sign-flip test (all 1024 sign patterns) as the decision rule, and a new R6.5 pre-registers ONE confirmatory endpoint (strategy vs matched-k vanilla, T=0.7, greedy, tau=0 superset) against the ~20-cell forking-paths exposure, with a required robustness row vs vanilla's best temperature. (4) RESULTS.md's documented headline commands were temperature-MISMATCHED (treatment silently inherited config T=1.0 while vanilla ran at 0.7) — an R2.4 violation in the repo's own reproduction instructions; fixed and R2.4 amended to require explicit temperature on both arms; config default recalibrated 1.0->0.7 (below the EntroPO Fig.4 whole-agent degradation knee, so the primary cannot manufacture a win from vanilla decoding degradation). (5) selected-pass@1 was claimed in the writeup with NO selector implementation anywhere; implemented the deployable majority-normalized-signature selector on both arms, tested, smoke-run on real artifacts (0.2222 on the legacy run). (6) Stated plainly, per the charter: at N=5 discrete semantic entropy is partition-quantized to exactly 7 values, so tau is a cluster-partition-shape rule, not a continuous dial, and tau=0 means 'branch iff >=2 clusters' — AND I proved the tau sweep needs ZERO extra GPU runs because the tau=0 run is the superset of every tau>0 run (the no-branch action keeps exactly the dominant-cluster representative trajectory, which exists in the superset run and executed greedily); scripts/tau_sweep.py implements the post-hoc sweep with the orchestrator's exact tie-break, unit-tested and smoke-verified on results/branching. Also resolved the trajectory-vs-token budget-match question in writing: trajectory-matching gives the CONTROL at least as much compute (treatment shares the SEARCH prefix), so it is the conservative match for treatment wins; token-matching would flatter the treatment and is correctly not used. Three spec amendments applied under ratchet v2 (R4.1/R4.2/R4.4 metric-time matching + rarefaction + deployable selector; R6.1/R6.5/R2.4 exact test + pre-registration + explicit temperature; R3.3 post-hoc sweep + quantization disclosure), each with rationale and rejected alternatives in spec_amendments/applied_03_*.md; none flips any item to pass for the existing artifact — all add obligations that were simultaneously implemented and tested. 63 tests pass (was 49 equivalent; +14 new), py_compile clean, all five driver --help smokes pass, compute_metrics and tau_sweep verified end-to-end on real artifacts. Because this iteration found and fixed real design flaws, gold_standard_met is FALSE per the scrutiny charter — the loop should pass once more over the post-amendment design; the GPU runs remain the human-only step.

issues_found.title: Matched-k enforced at run time but NOT at metric time: compare() differenced each arm's diverse-pass@k at its own k, biasing the gain whenever k_A != k_B (failed resamples, --max-k, capture loss)
issues_found.rationale: The matched-k design is the paper's central fairness device; a silent k divergence hands the larger arm a mechanical any-pass advantage. Fixed: both arms evaluated at common k*=min(k_A,k_B) via the Chen estimator, k-mismatched instances reported, demonstrated by a test where the naive comparison says 0 and the correct one says -0.5.

issues_found.title: RESULTS.md SS5 headline reproduction commands were temperature-mismatched (treatment silently at config T=1.0, vanilla at 0.7) — an R2.4 violation in the repo's own documentation
issues_found.rationale: Anyone following the documented procedure would produce a confounded headline comparison. Fixed the commands (explicit --temperature 0.7 on the treatment), amended R2.4 to require explicit temperature on both arms, and recalibrated the config default to the pre-registered primary T=0.7.

issues_found.title: selected-pass@1 claimed in RESULTS.md SS3 and the results table with NO selector implementation anywhere in the codebase
issues_found.rationale: An overclaim-in-waiting (R4.4). Implemented the majority normalized-patch-signature selector (self-consistency; deterministic tie-breaks; empty patches never win; all-empty = miss) — artifact-only and mechanism-independent so it runs identically on both arms. Tested + smoke-run on real artifacts.

issues_found.title: Inference at n=10 rested solely on a percentile bootstrap over lumpy 0/1 gains, across a ~20-cell sweep grid with no designated confirmatory comparison (forking-paths exposure)
issues_found.rationale: Percentile bootstrap of a mean of ten mostly {-1,0,1} values undercovers; and with dozens of cells, narrating the largest gain is not inference. Added the exact paired sign-flip test (1024 patterns) as the decision rule and a new R6.5 pre-registering one primary endpoint; all other cells labeled exploratory; robustness row vs vanilla's best temperature required.

issues_found.title: tau is partition-quantized at N=5 (7 achievable entropy values) — the gate is a cluster-partition-shape rule, and the headline tau=0 config gates only on 'any semantic split at all'
issues_found.rationale: Charter asked this be said plainly if true; it is true. Rather than pretend a continuous dial, the design now discloses the quantization, uses the achievable set as the tau grid, and exploits the superset property: the entire tau sweep is computed post-hoc from the tau=0 run by trajectory subsetting (scripts/tau_sweep.py) — same numbers a per-tau rerun would give, zero extra GPU cost. Keeping tau=0 for the headline is justified (the superset run strictly dominates); the disclosure closes the 'your gate never fires' attack.

issues_found.title: Cross-arm distinct-patch-count comparisons were sample-size biased at unequal k; off-mode recovery records lacked chance-level context; budget-match direction (trajectory vs token) was unstated
issues_found.rationale: Rarefaction estimator added for distinct counts (mean pairwise distance provably needs none — documented); off-mode records now carry both arms' (k, n_resolved) and the (1-p)^k caveat; RESULTS SS2.2 now states trajectory-matching is the conservative direction since the control receives at least as much compute.

issues_found.title: run_branching.py sample_temperature fallback bypassed cfg() (raw .get(..., 1.0))
issues_found.rationale: The exact single-source-of-truth divergence R8.2 exists to prevent — would have silently disagreed with the new 0.7 default. Routed through cfg().
